newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia expects $5 bln in foreign aid in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia expects $5 bln in foreign aid in 1997.

text.p: Indonesia expects to obtain some $5 billion in foreign aid this year and hopes its controversial national car policy will not hurt ties with key donor nations, Planning Minister Ginanjar Kartasasmita said on Thursday.
"We expect to receive around $5 billion in foreign aid. That is the amount expected by our planning side," Ginanjar told reporters after meeting President Suharto.
The funds will come from the World Bank-chaired Consultative Group for Indonesia (CGI), which consists of 20 donor countries, including Japan, and several financing agencies.
Ginanjar said the CGI will meet in Japan in July.
"I will visit Tokyo on June 9 to discuss Indonesia's development programme and Japan's aid in line with the coming meeting of the CGI," he said.
Ginanjar said he would not raise the issue of Indonesia's national car policy with Japan but would be ready to answer any questions on the issue if raised by Tokyo.

"I hope the Indonesia national car policy will not disturb or affect the economic relations between Indonesia and Japan, especially in the CGI. Until now I don't see it will hamper relations," he said.

Indonesia's national car policy gives PT Timor Putra Nasional, headed by President Suharto's youngest son Hutomo Mandala Putra, tax and tariff breaks to produce a national car in association with Kia Motors Corp of South Korea.
Japan, the United States and the European Union have said the policy discriminates against other car manufacturers and have brought their complaint to the World Trade Organisation.
Indonesia has defended its policy, citing the national car programme is aimed at strengthening its domestic industry.
The CGI pledged $5.26 billion in aid to Indonesia in 1996, compared with $5.35 billion in 1995. Of the total, Japan pledged $1.91 billion in 1996, compared with $2.14 billion in 1995.
Ginanjar said the funds would mainly be used to improve human resource development, infrastructure and alleviate poverty.
